result.title: EvoSkill-S1: Evolving Reusable Skills with Genetic-Inspired Operators
result.summary: Reusable skills allow language-model agents to accumulate and reuse problem-solving experience. However, most existing methods improve a skill bank only indirectly through rollout-driven accumulation and heuristic reflection, often resulting in shallow and weakly controlled updates. We present EvoSkill-S1, an RL-driven framework that instead treats reusable skills themselves as the direct objects of evolution. Given hard-negative failures, EvoSkill-S1 selects parent skills and transforms them into candidate child skills through five genetic-inspired operators: revision, cross-revision, mutation, dual-reflection, and crossover. Downstream task rewards train the skill evolver to generate more effective child skills, while evaluator-guided write-back selectively retains beneficial updates. Complementary Skill Bank Fusion consolidates operator-specific banks to exploit their distinct recovery patterns, while a Procedural Skill Interface supports transfer to unseen problems. Across all reported math and code benchmarks, EvoSkill-S1 improves the corresponding initialized skill banks under both Qwen and GPT-family solvers, with relative gains of up to 12.39%. Compared with the strongest external baseline without direct skill evolution, the largest relative improvement reaches 20.39%.

AI.brief_summary: EvoSkill-S1 研究语言模型智能体可复用技能库的进化式更新：以困难负例失败为输入，用五种遗传式算子（修订、交叉修订、变异、双重反思、交叉）由父技能生成子技能，并用下游任务奖励训练技能进化器，配合评估器引导的选择性写回与技能库融合。
AI.relevance_reason: 该文不涉及视觉状态或 latent 推理，但「候选技能生成—评估器筛选—选择性写回」的演化循环可能为 LVR 中多条 latent 假设的生成、筛选与保留提供类比线索，可供核查其筛选与贡献分配机制是否可迁移。
